title: SDKs, the REST API and the console as one client among several

videos.script: Click a button in the console, type a command, run a Python script. Each of them sends AWS the same thing. {{request}} It is an HTTPS request to a service, with a body that names an action, and a header that proves who sent it. {{signature}} That header is a signature. The secret key never leaves your computer. It signs a careful summary of the request, and AWS checks the result with its own copy. {{curl}} You will take one request apart, then send it again by hand with curl. {{protocols}} Then you will see that the services speak four dialects. Some take a form, some take JSON, and S3 uses the path itself. An SDK knows which is which. {{sdk}} You will run boto3, which has been in your lab since the first lesson. {{retries}} You will watch a client retry a failing call three times, and see why waiting longer each time matters. {{end}} And the course ends where the next ones begin. {{next}}
